title: UNIFIVE: Browser Pixel Game Studio
excerpt: UNIFIVE is an in-browser studio for creating 2D pixel games without installing software. It provides side-scrolling and top-down scene editing, visual block programming, sprite animation timelines, compressed single-file project exports, and mobile-ready play testing.
problem: Entry-level game engines require gigabyte-sized installations, account setups, or complex compile pipelines before beginners can build. Browser alternatives often lock projects into closed hosted platforms or lack multi-perspective camera support.
goal: Build a client-side game creation environment that runs in any modern browser without build steps, installations, or backend dependencies, while supporting both 2D platformer and top-down perspectives.
architecture: A static HTML and JavaScript application hosts a p5.js canvas workspace with a modular split interface for scene layout, visual block logic, and sprite properties. Dedicated modules manage canvas rendering, block code interpretation, Web Audio synthesis, and project serialization. Web Workers run gzip compression on project files in the background.
challenges: Executing a full scene editor, visual code interpreter, and animated sprite pipeline entirely client-side without stuttering the browser main thread.
solutions: Maintained isolated state stores for platformer versus top-down modes, batched canvas draw calls in a unified render loop, used the native Compression Streams API for single-file exports, and built a step-throttled block interpreter to prevent long-running loops from freezing the UI.
tradeOffs: A pure client-side architecture guarantees user privacy and zero hosting maintenance, but complex scenes with high entity counts depend strictly on client hardware performance.
lessons: Creative web tools stay responsive when rendering pipelines, visual scripting interpreters, and asset loaders have strict isolation boundaries and communicate through typed event buses.
outcome: A zero-install browser engine that allows students and developers to design, animate, play-test, and distribute complete pixel games as portable compressed files.

title: Queez CBT: Offline Examination Suite
excerpt: Queez CBT is an offline-first examination platform built for educational institutions and testing centers. The system coordinates three specialized applications over a local Wi-Fi network: an Express and SQLite host daemon, an Assessment Manager for test authoring, and a secured Student Portal with screen lockdown for desktop and Android.
problem: Standard web-based exam portals fail during internet downtime in school computer labs. Institutions also face risks of student screen switching, slow paper grading, and complex IP configurations in venues without dedicated IT administrators.
goal: Build an offline examination suite that supports complex STEM questions with KaTeX math rendering, enforces strict kiosk-mode screen lockdown, and synchronizes live test sessions over local Wi-Fi without internet connectivity.
architecture: A three-tier offline architecture comprising a central server host daemon, an Assessment Manager administration client, and a hardened Student Portal. The applications communicate over local subnets using UDP beacon discovery, REST endpoints, and WebSockets, writing exam records directly to embedded SQLite databases.
challenges: Preserving student response states during unstable Wi-Fi drops, preventing application window tampering on student computers, and rendering high-density mathematical notation without performance lag.
solutions: Implemented automatic subnet discovery using UDP broadcast beacons, native kiosk lockdown wrappers, an idempotent response queue backed by IndexedDB, and automatic shuffling of question orders and multiple-choice options per candidate.
tradeOffs: Maintaining separate desktop installers for Windows and APK builds for Android increases deployment build complexity compared to a single website, but guarantees continuous exam delivery during power or internet outages.
lessons: Critical testing environments demand defensive software design: offline storage fallback, deterministic state queues, and local network heartbeats are mandatory when remote internet cannot be trusted.
outcome: A production offline testing suite deployed in schools, featuring timed exam sessions, live hall proctoring, instant automated score calculation, printable candidate access slips, and branded PDF score reports.

title: Anonfly: Private Real-Time Messaging Platform
excerpt: Anonfly is an anonymous, end-to-end encrypted messaging platform comprising an API service, a React web client, and a developer SDK monorepo. It features disposable identity management, real-time message exchange over WebSockets and SSE, Redis pub/sub routing, and client integration packages for React, Next.js, and CLI environments.
problem: Ephemeral communication tools often require personal phone numbers or email logins, leaving persistent metadata trails. Furthermore, developers looking to integrate anonymous messaging lack modular SDKs for modern JavaScript frameworks.
goal: Build Anonfly as both an end-user chat product and an extensible open-source SDK, providing anonymous identity generation, encrypted message exchange, and clean developer integration packages.
architecture: The backend service coordinates session authorization, room presence, Redis pub/sub messaging channels, and encrypted message persistence. The client manages in-browser cryptographic keys and real-time chat views. A Turborepo monorepo publishes core, React, Next.js, and CLI client libraries.
challenges: Maintaining sub-50ms message latency across concurrent chat rooms while securing disposable tokens and ensuring clean monorepo package versioning.
solutions: Implemented Redis pub/sub to fan out messages across WebSocket server instances, enforced cryptographic signature verification on incoming sockets, and used Turborepo with Changesets to publish independent client libraries.
tradeOffs: Dividing the architecture into distinct backend, client, and package packages adds build orchestration overhead, but allows third-party developers to embed Anonfly capabilities into outside applications.
lessons: Security-focused platforms stay maintainable when core cryptographic primitives, transport layers, and user interface components are decoupled into isolated packages.
outcome: A complete encrypted real-time chat platform with disposable room codes, sub-50ms message delivery, and published SDK packages for frontend and Node.js integrations.

title: WorkUp Cards: Business Card Generator
excerpt: WorkUp Cards is an in-browser business card designer that allows users to pick curated templates, edit front and back details in real time, inspect card layouts, and export high-resolution printable PNG images directly on the client.
problem: Freelancers and business owners needing quick professional cards must often purchase complex graphic design suites or wait for server-side rendering tools that introduce latency and privacy concerns.
goal: Deliver a fast, browser-first card builder with customizable layout templates, instantaneous live rendering, and client-side raster export ready for printing.
architecture: A React application where form inputs synchronize with SVG and HTML card layouts. Form state is validated via Zod schemas, while a dedicated canvas exporter renders card elements into high-density raster images directly in the browser.
challenges: Rendering complex vector layouts and custom typography onto canvas buffers without font-clipping or blurriness on high-DPI displays.
solutions: Applied structured CSS print dimensions, debounced render passes during live form editing, and scaled html2canvas capture buffers by device pixel ratios for sharp exports.
tradeOffs: Generating exports client-side eliminates server hosting bills, but older mobile devices require careful memory management when rasterizing high-resolution images.
lessons: Interactive graphics tools feel instantaneous when form state updates and canvas capture triggers are clearly separated and debounced.
outcome: A fast, client-side business card generator featuring multiple design templates, responsive previews, and instant PNG downloads without backend dependencies.

title: WorldTimeSage: Global Timezone Dashboard
excerpt: WorldTimeSage is an interactive global timezone dashboard and reference tool. It includes searchable world clocks, country timezone inspections, timezone offset comparisons, offline availability, and installable Progressive Web App (PWA) support.
problem: Remote professionals coordinating across global time zones need more than basic clock apps. They require instant country lookups, daylight saving indicators, and offline access while traveling.
goal: Build an intuitive timezone dashboard with search, regional offset comparisons, custom location pins, and full offline functionality as an installable PWA.
architecture: A modular Single Page Application built with React and Redux Toolkit. Features are partitioned into dashboard, country details, offline caches, and settings views, utilizing Service Workers to cache geographical datasets.
challenges: Accurately calculating localized time offsets and daylight saving adjustments across disparate regions while keeping the UI responsive and lightweight.
solutions: Leveraged native Intl.DateTimeFormat browser APIs to minimize third-party bundle weight, indexed location data for instant search queries, and configured service worker caching for offline access.
tradeOffs: Providing extensive geographical metadata increases initial cache size, but ensures all timezone lookups continue to work without internet connectivity.
lessons: PWA utilities benefit from utilizing native browser platform APIs like Intl before reaching for heavy external date libraries.
outcome: An installable timezone dashboard with sub-second country search, multi-city comparison clocks, and offline support for distributed teams.

title: AsterMail: Dynamic Email Delivery API
excerpt: AsterMail is a lightweight backend email service that dispatches transactional messages through dynamic SMTP credentials. The API provides input validation, rate limiting, request logging, in-memory caching, and structured error responses for developer applications.
problem: Developers building lightweight apps often need to send transactional emails without signing up for expensive enterprise email platforms or hardcoding static SMTP credentials into their primary repositories.
goal: Build a secure REST API capable of validating email payloads, configuring SMTP transports dynamically per request, and returning uniform status responses.
architecture: An Express 5 microservice structured with strict input validation middleware, on-demand Nodemailer transport factories, Helmet security headers, and LRU memory caching to limit redundant transport initializations.
challenges: Preventing abuse from unauthorized senders while maintaining fast email delivery and clean error reporting when external mail servers reject credentials.
solutions: Enforced strict payload validation using Express Validator, applied IP-based rate limiting, standardized HTTP error schemas, and pooled transport connections using LRU caching.
tradeOffs: Accepting dynamic credentials gives client apps total transport flexibility, but demands rigorous input sanitization to guard against email header injection attacks.
lessons: Backend microservices stay reliable when operational concerns like logging, transport pooling, and security middleware are standardized at the root router level.
outcome: A production email microservice handling dynamic SMTP delivery, automated input validation, and structured error handling for web applications.

title: Geemex: Gaming Landing Page Template
excerpt: Geemex is a modern gaming community and title showcase landing page built with Vue 3 and Vite. It features character showcase carousels, responsive pricing tiers, interactive FAQ accordions, and action-driven CTA banners tailored for indie games and gaming brands.
problem: Indie game studios and tournament organizers often lack the time to build bespoke marketing pages, yet generic templates fail to capture the high-contrast aesthetic required for gaming titles.
goal: Create a performant, modular gaming landing page template that pairs expressive game-inspired visuals with fast load times and clean component code.
architecture: A Vue 3 Single Page Application using Vite 6 and Tailwind CSS 4. Organized into discrete Single File Components for hero, character spotlights, tier pricing, community FAQs, and download links.
challenges: Delivering high-contrast gaming aesthetics with fluid micro-interactions without causing layout shifts or slowing mobile load performance.
solutions: Constructed lightweight CSS transitions for interactive cards and character hover states, optimized asset delivery via Vite's build pipeline, and enforced strict TypeScript typing across all component props.
tradeOffs: Focusing on a static marketing layout keeps execution fast and maintenance minimal, but dynamic tournament registration requires adding a backend API.
lessons: Themed marketing templates succeed when typography, layout hierarchy, and reusable component slots allow developers to customize branding in minutes.
outcome: A lightweight, production-ready gaming template featuring modular Vue 3 components, fast load times, and responsive layouts across all screen resolutions.

title: Asterixh School: Educational Portal & Admissions Hub
excerpt: Asterixh School is an informative school website and digital admissions portal. Built with Next.js 16 App Router and TypeScript, it presents academic curriculums, event notice boards, admission criteria, and interactive inquiry forms in a structured multi-page experience.
problem: Prospective parents and students frequently struggle to find admission dates, fee structures, and curriculum details on outdated school websites that render poorly on mobile screens.
goal: Develop a fast, modern school portal that highlights educational values, streamlines admissions inquiries, and renders flawlessly on mobile and desktop devices.
architecture: Next.js App Router powers server-rendered pages for academics, admissions, faculty, and news. Interactive enrollment and contact forms use client-side validation, supported by shared header, navigation, and footer components.
challenges: Organizing extensive academic information across multiple grade levels while preserving an uncluttered visual hierarchy and rapid page transitions.
solutions: Implemented a clean information architecture with clear navigation categories, breadcrumbs, card grids for curriculum highlights, and Zod-validated application forms.
tradeOffs: Using static file-based routing ensures rapid page loads, but dynamic student grade lookups would require an administrative backend.
lessons: Institutional websites work best when key actions, like submitting an admission inquiry or viewing term dates, are accessible within two clicks from the homepage.
outcome: A mobile-responsive school portal delivering fast page loads, clear admission guidelines, and organized academic information for prospective families.

title: SMS: School Management System
excerpt: SMS is a full-stack educational management platform with decoupled frontend and backend architectures. It features role-based access control, attendance tracking, student profiles, academic conduct records, and financial workflows backed by Express, PostgreSQL, and Supabase.
problem: School administrators often juggle disconnected spreadsheets and paper files for student records, daily attendance, fee tracking, and staff duties, causing data errors and audit delays.
goal: Build an integrated management system where administrators, teachers, and bursars operate from a unified platform with strict role-based access boundaries.
architecture: The frontend uses React Router, React Query, and Zustand for state caching across administrative modules. The backend exposes modular Express services for authentication, student rosters, attendance tracking, conduct records, and tuition receipts, writing to PostgreSQL hosted on Supabase.
challenges: Enforcing granular permissions across multiple operational views while keeping frontend routing aligned with backend authorization middleware.
solutions: Defined strict role-based navigation guards on the client, verified access tokens and role claims at each API route, and optimized database queries with foreign key constraints and indexes.
tradeOffs: Separating frontend and backend repositories introduces API contract synchronization requirements, but allows independent scaling and continuous deployment of each tier.
lessons: Role-aware platforms remain stable when access permissions are modeled as core business rules in the database rather than simple client-side conditional checks.
outcome: A structured school operations system supporting student enrolment, daily attendance recording, tuition verification, and role-based staff administration.

title: motion-lyte.js: Declarative Web Animation Library
excerpt: motion-lyte.js is a lightweight, framework-agnostic animation library driven by declarative HTML data attributes. It provides scroll, hover, and toggle triggers, includes a dedicated React hook and Vite plugin, and adds zero runtime bundle overhead for basic interactions.
problem: Many animation packages require heavy JavaScript runtimes or complex imperative setup code that clutters frontend templates and degrades initial page load performance.
goal: Develop a lightweight animation utility that lets engineers attach performant motion behaviors directly using HTML data attributes, while offering modern React and Vite integrations.
architecture: A lightweight runtime scanning DOM elements with data-motion attributes, powered by Intersection Observer for scroll triggers. Ships with a core engine, custom TypeScript definitions, a React wrapper hook, and a Vite plugin bundled using tsup.
challenges: Designing an expressive declarative attribute syntax while supporting staggered delays, configurable easing curves, and dynamic scroll intersection thresholds.
solutions: Constructed an internal motion registry mapping data attributes to hardware-accelerated CSS transforms, coupled with pooled Intersection Observers to eliminate layout thrashing.
tradeOffs: Declarative HTML data attributes enable rapid adoption and minimal footprint, but complex multi-timeline choreographies still favor imperative animation libraries like GSAP.
lessons: Open-source developer tools gain adoption when they provide instant zero-config HTML usage alongside typed framework wrappers for React and Vite.
outcome: An open-source web animation library with under 4KB runtime footprint, automated Vitest test coverage, and drop-in integration for static and React sites.

title: Catalyst Consultant: Business Consulting Landing Page
excerpt: Catalyst Consultant is a conversion-focused marketing landing page for a business advisory firm. Delivered as a static Vite site with custom CSS and motion-lyte.js, it presents services, consultant profiles, client testimonials, transparent pricing, and direct consultation booking forms.
problem: Consulting agencies struggle to convey credibility and convert web visitors into qualified client bookings when using sluggish, bloated theme templates.
goal: Build a high-performance one-page consulting site combining persuasive copy hierarchy, micro-interactions, and rapid static delivery to maximize booking conversions.
architecture: A static Vite architecture delivering pre-rendered HTML and optimized CSS assets. `motion-lyte.js` powers subtle scroll reveals and hover states on cards, testimonials, and consultation booking forms.
challenges: Maintaining an engaging, premium visual presentation with interactive accordions and carousels while keeping page weight minimal and initial paint times under one second.
solutions: Structured sections with clear visual hierarchy, applied declarative motion attributes to key headlines and statistics, and implemented responsive appointment inquiry forms.
tradeOffs: A static architecture maximizes page load speeds and eliminates server vulnerabilities, but dynamic client intake scheduling requires third-party calendar or webhook integration.
lessons: Conversion-focused landing pages succeed when value propositions are stated above the fold and reinforced with social proof, transparent pricing, and low-friction CTAs.
outcome: A responsive consulting marketing page that delivers sub-second load times and serves as a practical showcase for the motion-lyte.js animation library.

title: Resin Art: Creative Portfolio & Product Catalog
excerpt: Resin Art is a product showcase portfolio and customer inquiry storefront for artisanal resin crafts. Built with Next.js 16 and TypeScript, it pairs rich visual galleries and product catalogs with automated email inquiry routing and direct WhatsApp order channels.
problem: Artisanal creators need more than flat photo galleries to grow sales. They require structured product catalogs, credibility signals, and direct messaging channels to quote custom commissions without expensive e-commerce platform fees.
goal: Deliver an elegant portfolio and catalog experience that showcases handmade resin pieces and connects interested buyers directly to WhatsApp and email order flows.
architecture: Next.js App Router manages layout and dynamic catalog views. Structured JSON files drive product specifications and testimonials, while API routes validate custom commission inquiries using Zod and Nodemailer.
challenges: Balancing high-resolution artisan photography with fast mobile load speeds, and creating an effortless mobile handoff to WhatsApp for custom order quotes.
solutions: Utilized Next.js image optimization with modern webp formats, structured categorical filtering, and added direct click-to-chat WhatsApp triggers pre-filled with product names.
tradeOffs: A catalog and lead generation model is ideal for custom-made bespoke items, but high-volume standard product inventory would eventually require an automated payment checkout.
lessons: For handmade and custom goods, direct conversational checkout via WhatsApp converts higher than complex multi-step shopping carts.
outcome: A mobile-first brand portfolio and product catalog generating qualified custom order inquiries via automated email routing and WhatsApp integration.
